perf.summary: Computes Math.Sqrt for every one of the O(n^2) pairs; if S is used only for separation comparisons the sqrt can be deferred or avoided.
perf.currentCost: Inner loop runs Math.Sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy) for all n(n-1)/2 pairs. sqrt is ~15-20+ cycle latency and serializes the loop; for n=1000 that is ~500k sqrts.
perf.proposedChange: If downstream consumers compare/threshold distances, store squared distance (dx*dx+dy*dy) in S and compare against squared thresholds, eliminating sqrt entirely. If the true distance is required, at least the loop is embarrassingly parallel — structure dx/dy as SoA spans so Burst can vectorize the multiply-add, and only sqrt the surviving pairs.
perf.rationale: Dropping sqrt removes the dominant per-pair latency in an O(n^2) kernel; squared-distance comparisons are monotonic so thresholding is exact without the root.
perf.risk: Changing S to squared distance changes the observable field value — only valid if all consumers are updated to expect squared (state guard: confirm no caller reads S as Euclidean distance). If S must remain true distance, keep sqrt but vectorize.

perf.summary: This is a brute-force all-pairs enumeration (O(n^2) pairs), not a Well-Separated Pair Decomposition, which produces O(n) pairs via a split-tree.
perf.currentCost: Emits every pair: count = n(n-1)/2 = O(n^2) pairs and O(n^2) work and output RAM. A real WSPD over a fair-split tree yields O(n) pairs for fixed separation s in O(n log n) build time.
perf.proposedChange: Implement the actual WSPD: build a fair-split / kd tree, then recursively emit well-separated node pairs using the separation ratio s, producing O(s^d * n) pairs. This matches the class name Wspd and slashes both time and the pairs[] output size from quadratic to near-linear.
perf.rationale: Genuine asymptotic improvement (O(n^2)->O(n log n) time, O(n^2)->O(n) output) and correct WSPD semantics; the separation parameter s is currently stored but never used to prune, confirming the current code is a placeholder.
perf.risk: Large algorithmic change and changes output (set of pairs and their meaning) — flag for owner. Current code ignores s for pruning, so output differs from a true WSPD; treat as feature-completion, not a behavior-preserving micro-opt.
